title: One Indexed Query Replaces a 20,000-Row Scan on /news | vitalii.no
description:
The idea was simple: draw one country flag per page load in the last five minutes, so two readers from China show two Chinese flags, and put a 'most read' strip above /news and /blog. Building it exposed a real performance wall - the first version matched articles to page paths with a slug IN-list, and that correlated subquery re-scanned all roughly 20,000 rows in the news table for every single path, blowing straight through the 3-second anonymous statement timeout on the database.

A Cloudflare Worker now returns country codes alongside its visitor counters, and the live badge draws one flag emoji per unique visit in the last five minutes instead of a plain count. For the 'most read' feature, a plain SQL function joins articles to aggregated view counts through a proper slug table instead of a correlated IN-clause, turning a full table rescan into a single indexed join. The strip renders above both blog and news listings with a 7 day / 30 day / all-time switch - the 30-day window is server-rendered, the other two are fetched on click.

The most-read strip now answers from a single indexed function call instead of a 20,000-row rescan per path, so it no longer risks the 3-second timeout that would have made the whole listing page fail to render.
